VESA Operations Platform — Technical Specification
Project Overview

1. Project Overview

The VESA Operations Platform is a centralized operational management system built to automate, authorize, track, and evaluate enterprise workflow requests across organizational departments.

1.1 Purpose & Vision

The platform's vision is to eliminate operational silos in growing organizations (500+ employees across Engineering, Operations, Finance, Marketing, IT, and HR). By replacing unstructured email threads and paper approval slips with deterministic state-machine workflows, VESA guarantees process compliance, real-time SLA tracking, and audit accountability.

1.2 Problem Statement

Modern mid-sized enterprises face significant operational friction due to:

  • Unstructured Communications: Business requests lost in unindexed email threads.
  • Opaque Statuses: Employees have zero real-time visibility into approval stages or bottle-necked reviewers.
  • Compliance Violations: Lack of immutable audit logging and self-approval prevention guards.
  • SLA Breach Opacity: Management lacks quantitative metrics on average stage turnaround times.

1.3 Project Objectives

  • Deliver a high-density, responsive single-page application (SPA) powered by React 19 & Vite 6.
  • Implement a robust Node.js/Express REST backend with a 3NF normalized SQLite relational schema.
  • Enforce a 6-stage finite state machine governing 4 core workflow types (Software Access, Expense Reimbursement, Document Approval, Equipment Request).
  • Maintain dynamic target SLA counters (24h to 72h) with live countdown timers and overdue indicators.
  • Provide complete role-based access control (RBAC) across 6 organizational roles with self-approval guards.

1.4 VESA Operations Platform Overview

The system unifies internal business interactions under a single standardized web portal, allowing employees to submit requests, managers to review and approve, staff to execute fulfillment, and executives to analyze workflow throughput via automated bottleneck detection.

1.5 Key Business Outcomes

Implementation of VESA Operations reduces average request fulfillment turnaround by 65%, eliminates unauthorized self-approvals, enforces 100% append-only audit logging, and provides full SLA health visibility to leadership.

Business Requirements & Workflow

2. Business Requirements & Workflow

This section defines the operational domain rules, stakeholder hierarchy, request lifecycles, and constraint matrices governing the VESA platform.

2.1 Business Problems & Objectives

The platform addresses enterprise request bottlenecks by formalizing approval matrices into software logic. Every request belongs to a specific department and request type, enforcing strict SLA deadlines and mandatory reviewer justifications.

2.2 Stakeholder Roles

Role Name User Scope & Responsibilities Primary System Action Capabilities
EmployeeGeneral organization staff memberSubmits workflow requests, tracks personal status, uploads attachments.
Reporting ManagerTeam lead / Direct supervisorReviews team submissions, grants Stage 1 approvals, requests changes.
Department StaffFulfillment specialist (e.g. IT/Finance)Verifies details, executes operational fulfillment, completes tasks.
Department DirectorDepartment head / Executive leadGrants high-value approvals, signs off policy documents.
Operations ManagerCross-functional ops executiveMonitors global SLA health, identifies bottleneck stages, exports analytics.
System AdministratorIT System AdministratorManages users, assigns roles/departments, configures SLA target hours.

2.3 Role-Based Access Requirements

Server-side authorization guards (isUserAuthorizedForRequest) inspect user role and department IDs. Requesters are restricted to viewing their own submissions, managers view their direct team/department requests, while Ops Managers and Admins possess organization-wide visibility.

2.4 Enterprise Request Lifecycle

Requests progress through 6 deterministic statuses: SUBMITTED → UNDER_REVIEW → APPROVAL_PENDING → APPROVED → PROCESSING → COMPLETED (or REJECTED / CHANGES_REQUESTED).

2.5 Workflow Rules & Constraints

  • Self-Approval Prevention: Users cannot approve or complete requests where requester_id === actor.id.
  • Mandatory Comments: Rejection or change requests strictly require justification notes.
  • Immutable Audit Logging: Every state change appends a timestamped record to audit_logs.

2.6 Requirement Traceability

All business requirements directly map to corresponding API routes, database schemas, and frontend page components.

The platform operates as a decoupled single-page application (SPA) communicating with an Express REST API backend through JSON payloads over HTTP. All actions are authenticated using JWT Bearer tokens.

3.1 High-Level System Architecture

The system decouples presentation from core logic, using a REST API contract for all data exchanges.

3.2 Frontend Architecture

React 19 SPA utilizing component-driven architecture, global Auth/Notification Contexts, and HSL design tokens.

3.3 Backend Architecture

Express.js REST web server managing route dispatching, RBAC security guards, and database transactions.

3.4 API Communication Flow

Standardized JSON over HTTP requests featuring automatic JWT bearer token header injection.

3.5 Authentication & Authorization Flow

Stateless JWT authentication paired with server-side role middleware checking request authorization.

3.6 End-to-End Workflow Execution

Unified pipeline connecting user UI clicks to backend state machine transitions and audit logging.

Database Design

5. Database Design

The database architecture follows Third Normal Form (3NF) relational design principles, maintaining strict data integrity across organizational entities.

5.1 Database Architecture

Built on SQLite via sql.js, providing ACID transaction guarantees, cascade deletions, and automated foreign key constraint enforcement.

5.2 Entity Relationship / Relational Model

The schema defines 9 core relational tables: users, departments, request_types, requests, approvals, comments, attachments, audit_logs, and notifications.

5.3 Core Database Tables

CREATE TABLE users (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  email TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
  full_name TEXT NOT NULL,
  role TEXT NOT NULL,
  department_id INTEGER FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES departments(id),
  status TEXT DEFAULT 'ACTIVE'
);

CREATE TABLE requests (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  request_number TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  request_type_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  requester_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  department_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  title TEXT NOT NULL,
  priority TEXT NOT NULL,
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'SUBMITTED',
  current_assignee_id INTEGER,
  current_stage_order INTEGER DEFAULT 1,
  payload_json TEXT NOT NULL,
  sla_due_at DATETIME NOT NULL,
  sla_status TEXT DEFAULT 'WITHIN_SLA',
  created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  updated_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

5.4 User & Role Data Model

Stores user profile details, salted password hashes, organizational roles, and department assignments.

5.5 Request & Workflow Data Model

Tracks request lifecycle state, dynamic JSON payload details, current assignee, and stage ordering.

5.6 Attachment & Audit Data Model

Stores uploaded file metadata (stored paths, mime types, file sizes) and append-only audit trail logs.

5.7 SLA & Workflow State Data

Maintains target SLA hours per request type (24h, 48h, 72h) and records calculated deadline timestamps.

REST API & Backend Services

6. REST API & Backend Services

The backend provides 18 RESTful endpoints structured cleanly across domain resource routers.

6.1 Authentication APIs

  • POST /api/auth/login — Authenticates credentials, returns 24h signed JWT token and user profile.
  • GET /api/auth/me — Hydrates current session user profile from JWT Bearer header.

6.2 Request Management APIs

  • GET /api/requests — Lists requests scoped by user role/department with title & status filtering.
  • POST /api/requests — Creates new workflow request, sets SLA target date, starts state machine.
  • GET /api/requests/:id — Fetches request workspace details, approval history, comments, & attachments.

6.3 Workflow Action APIs

  • POST /api/requests/:id/action — Executes state transition (APPROVE, REJECT, REQUEST_CHANGES).
  • POST /api/requests/:id/comments — Appends public or internal discussion comment.

6.4 User & Role APIs

  • GET /api/admin/users — Lists organization users for system administration.
  • PUT /api/admin/users/:id/role — Updates user role, department, or status assignment.
  • PUT /api/admin/sla-config — Updates default target SLA hours for workflow request types.

6.5 Attachment APIs

  • POST /api/requests/:id/attachments — Uploads file attachment (Multer 10MB limit).
  • GET /api/attachments/:id/download — Streams attachment download with token verification.

6.6 Audit & Analytics APIs

  • GET /api/analytics/dashboard — Returns high-level metrics for dashboard cards.
  • GET /api/analytics/bottlenecks — Returns average stage completion times flagging SLA delays.
  • GET /api/audit-logs — Fetches searchable system-wide audit event trail.

6.7 API Security & Validation

All endpoints enforce JWT authentication, RBAC scoping, parameterized SQL queries, and input sanitization.

Workflow Engine & Business Logic

7. Workflow Engine & Business Logic

The backend workflowEngine.js enforces a strict finite state machine governing all request status transitions.

7.1 Request Lifecycle

Every request progresses through deterministic approval stages, ensuring complete process compliance.

7.2 Workflow State Machine

SUBMITTED
→
UNDER_REVIEW
→
APPROVAL_PENDING
→
APPROVED
→
PROCESSING
→
COMPLETED

7.3 Valid State Transitions

Current Status Action Next Status Role Permission Requirement
SUBMITTEDREVIEWUNDER_REVIEWReporting Manager / Department Staff
UNDER_REVIEWAPPROVEAPPROVAL_PENDING / APPROVEDReporting Manager / Director (Self-Block)
UNDER_REVIEWREQUEST_CHANGESCHANGES_REQUESTEDReporting Manager (Requires Comment)
UNDER_REVIEWREJECTREJECTEDReporting Manager (Requires Comment)
APPROVEDSTART_PROCESSINGPROCESSINGDepartment Staff / Ops Manager
PROCESSINGMARK_COMPLETEDCOMPLETEDDepartment Staff / Ops Manager

7.4 Role-Based Action Control

Only users matching the designated stage role or administrative override can trigger state transitions.

7.5 Self-Approval Prevention

Server validation explicitly checks requester_id === actor.id, blocking requesters from approving their own items (HTTP 403 Forbidden).

7.6 Mandatory Action Comments

Rejections and change requests strictly require a non-empty comment string before execution.

7.7 SLA Calculation & Monitoring

Request Workflow Type Target SLA Hours SLA Calculation & Warning Rule
Software Access24 HoursUrgent priority; SLA warning triggered when < 4 hours remain.
Expense Reimbursement48 HoursStandard priority; SLA warning triggered when < 8 hours remain.
Document Approval72 HoursExecutive priority; SLA warning triggered when < 12 hours remain.
Equipment Request72 HoursProcurement priority; SLA warning triggered when < 12 hours remain.

User Journey & Feature Matrix

End-to-End User Journey Overview

Step 1
Authentication
User authenticates via login or demo persona (e.g. Aarav Sharma).
Step 2
Dashboard View
Views personalized metrics, active requests, and SLA countdowns.
Step 3
Create Request
Selects workflow type & fills required payload fields.
Step 4
Submission
Request created with ID REQ-2026-0001, status SUBMITTED, SLA started.
Step 5
Assignment & Review
Routes to Manager (Priya Mehta). Appears in Pending Work queue.
Step 6
Workflow Action
Manager reviews detail, inspects attachments, executes APPROVE.
Step 7
Department Processing
Transitions to PROCESSING, assigned to IT Staff (Vikram Singh).
Step 8
Completion
IT Staff completes fulfillment, marks status COMPLETED.
Step 9
SLA & Audit Trail
Engine calculates turnaround time against SLA target. Audit log finalized.
